_readme: Phish or Legit messages. kind: email | url | sms. answer: phish | legit. Every clue's `text` must appear word for word in from, subject, body or url: the TV highlights it on the reveal. `context` (optional) is a line of background shown above the message. Company and brand names here are made up.

items.subject: Unusual sign-in activity
items.body:
We detected a sign-in to your account from an unrecognised device in another country. If this wasn't you, verify your identity within 24 hours or your mailbox will be suspended.

Verify now: http://megasoft-365-alerts.com/verify

clues.why: Not megasoft.com. A look-alike domain with extra words bolted on.
A deadline and a threat, so you rush.
A 'security' link without HTTPS.

items.subject: Planned maintenance: Saturday 6am to 9am
items.body:
The VPN and file shares will be offline on Saturday from 6am to 9am while we patch the servers. You don't need to do anything.

Questions? Reply here or open a ticket in the IT portal.

clues.why: Your own company's real domain.

clues.text: You don't need to do anything
clues.why: No link, no login, no attachment.

clues.text: open a ticket in the IT portal
clues.why: Points you to the usual channel.

items.body: PayPortal: Log in to your account

clues.why: The real domain is the last part before the first single slash: secure-login.info. 'payportal.com' is just a subdomain decoration.

items.body: Kestrel Bank: Sign in to Online Banking

clues.why: The domain is exactly the bank's own, followed by a normal path.
A secure connection.

items.body: ParcelDash: Your parcel is on hold due to an unpaid $1.99 customs fee. Pay now to avoid return: parceldash-redelivery.top/pay

clues.why: A tiny fee is bait to get your card details.
Not the courier's domain, on a cheap throwaway ending.
A random personal number, not the company's usual sender.

items.context: You just tried to sign in to CodeVault.
items.body: Your CodeVault verification code is 418 207. It expires in 10 minutes. Don't share it with anyone. CodeVault will never ask for it.

clues.why: Warns you off sharing, and there's no link.
The service's usual short code, and you were expecting it.

items.subject: Quick favour
items.body: Are you at your desk? I need you to buy 5 x $200 gift cards for a client today. Keep this between us for now, it's a surprise. Email me the codes as soon as you have them. I'm in meetings so I can't take calls.

clues.why: Your CEO's personal-looking address, not the company one.
The classic scam payout: untraceable and instant.
Secrecy stops you checking with anyone.
Blocks the obvious way to verify.

items.subject: Your monthly invoice is ready
items.context: Your team pays for CloudCrate storage.
items.body:
Hi Pinecrest team,
Your CloudCrate invoice for October ($240.00) is ready. It will be charged to the card ending 4417 on file on Nov 5.
View it any time under Billing at cloudcrate.io.

clues.why: The vendor's real domain.
Details you'd recognise, and it asks for nothing.
Tells you to go to the site yourself instead of clicking.

items.subject: 2026 Salary Adjustment: ACTION REQUIRED
items.body:
Please review your updated salary details in the attached document and sign by end of day.

Attachment: Salary_Review_2026.html

clues.why: A look-alike of pinecrest.co.
Shouty urgency.
An HTML attachment usually opens a fake login page.

items.body: MegaSoft account: Reset your password

clues.why: A zero where the letter o should be.
A password page with no HTTPS.

items.body: CodeVault: Security settings

clues.why: The real domain, then an ordinary settings path.

items.body: KESTREL ALERT: A payment of $2,450.00 to J. MORRIS was approved. If you did NOT make this, call our fraud team now on 1-888-555-0143.

clues.text: call our fraud team now on 1-888-555-0143
clues.why: Call the number on the back of your card, never one from the message.
A scary amount to make you panic.
Sender names on texts are easy to fake.

items.subject: Invitation: Sprint review @ Thu 2pm
items.context: Priya is on your team, and your team uses TalkLoop.
items.body:
Priya Shah has invited you to Sprint review.
Thursday 2:00pm to 2:45pm
Join from the TalkLoop app, or accept from your calendar.

clues.why: The real sender domain for an app you use.
Someone you know, about a meeting you'd expect.
No odd links or attachments.

items.subject: Mailbox full: 98% used
items.body:
Your mailbox has exceeded its storage limit. Incoming mail will be rejected. Click below and log in to increase your quota for free.

[ Increase quota ]

clues.why: The real domain is support-desk.net, not pinecrest.co.

clues.text: log in to increase your quota
clues.why: IT never needs your password to give you more space.
Fear of missing mail, to rush you.

items.subject: Practice phishing results: well done!
items.body:
Last week's practice phishing email was reported by 82% of staff. Thank you!
Keep using the Report button in your mail app for anything suspicious.

clues.why: Your own company's domain.
Points to a built-in tool. No link to click.

items.body: CloudCrate: Sign in to view this shared file

clues.why: The real domain is io-share.com. 'cloudcrate' is just decoration.
A login wall on a 'shared file' is a classic password grab.

items.body: Pinecrest Help Center: How to set up the VPN

clues.why: A subdomain of your company's real domain.

items.body: Hi Mum, I dropped my phone in the bath, this is my new number. Can you help me pay a bill today? I'll pay you back tomorrow x

clues.why: 'New number' plus a money request: call the old number to check.
An urgent payment request.

items.subject: New SSH key added to your account
items.body:
Someone added a new SSH key to your account. If this wasn't you, revoke it here:
https://codevault.dev.revoke-key.co/session

clues.why: The link goes to revoke-key.co, not codevault.dev.
The sender looks right, but sender addresses can be faked. Always check the link.

items.subject: Your order is out for delivery
items.context: You ordered a laptop stand on Monday.
items.body:
Order #PD-48213 from Gadget Outlet is out for delivery today between 1pm and 4pm.
Track it in the ParcelDash app.

clues.why: The courier's real domain.

clues.text: Track it in the ParcelDash app
clues.why: No payment and no link: just the app you already have.

items.subject: You are eligible for a tax refund of $612.40
items.body: After the annual calculation of your fiscal activity we have determined that you are eligible to receive a tax refund of $612.40. Please submit the form with your card details to receive your refund within 3 business days.

clues.why: Tax offices don't use .com look-alike domains.
Refunds never need your card number.
Odd, stiff wording is common in scams.

items.context: You just paid Sam back for lunch.
items.body: PayPortal: You sent $25.00 to Sam Lee. Not you? Open the PayPortal app to review.

clues.why: Matches exactly what you just did.
Sends you to the app, not a link.

items.body: Kestrel Bank: Online Banking

clues.why: The number 1 instead of the letter l.

items.body: Pinecrest Single Sign-On

clues.why: Browsers ignore everything before the @. This goes to a bare IP address.

items.body: PayPortal: Account summary

clues.why: Exactly the real domain, with an ordinary path.

items.subject: You have 3 unread voice messages
items.body:
You received a voicemail (0:42) from +1 212 555 0177.
Play the message: Voicemail_0042.htm

clues.why: Not megasoft.com.
Voicemails aren't web pages. An .htm attachment is a fake login.
Curiosity bait.

items.subject: Your November payslip is available
items.body: Your payslip is ready in the HR portal. For your security we don't attach payslips or include links. Sign in to the HR portal as usual to view it.

clues.why: Your company's real domain.

clues.text: we don't attach payslips or include links
clues.why: Exactly what a careful sender does.

items.subject: New parking permits: scan to register
items.body:
All staff must re-register for parking by Friday. Scan the QR code below with your phone and sign in with your work account.

[ QR CODE ]

clues.why: A look-alike of pinecrest.co.

clues.text: sign in with your work account
clues.why: Parking doesn't need your work password.
QR codes hide the link and move you to your less protected phone.

items.context: You logged a ticket about your laptop yesterday.
items.body: Pinecrest IT: Ticket #8812 'Laptop won't charge' is resolved. Reply 1 if it's still broken.

clues.why: Matches the ticket you actually logged.
No link, no login, nothing to pay.

items.body: MegaSoft Support: We detected a virus on your PC. Call us now at 1-844-555-0190 so a technician can connect remotely and remove it.

clues.text: We detected a virus on your PC
clues.why: Nobody outside can see viruses on your computer.
Remote access lets them take over your PC.
Big software companies don't text you from personal numbers.

items.subject: [pinecrest/web] Pull request #212 merged
items.context: You opened pull request #212 this morning.
items.body:
alex-k merged #212 'Fix login redirect' into main.
View it on codevault.dev, or turn off these notifications in Settings.

clues.why: The pull request you actually opened.
Sends you to the real site, and asks for nothing.

items.subject: Pinecrest Contract: Signature needed (2 documents)
items.context: You don't know anyone called Gary Holt.
items.body:
Gary Holt has sent you 2 documents to review and sign.

[ REVIEW DOCUMENTS ]

This link expires in 4 hours.

clues.why: A stranger sending you a contract out of the blue.
A countdown to rush you.
An odd domain for an e-signature service.

items.context: Priya said in chat that she just shared the budget with you.
items.body: CloudCrate: Q3_Budget.xlsx shared with you by Priya Shah

clues.why: The real domain, with a short share link.

clues.text: shared with you by Priya Shah
clues.why: Expected: Priya told you it was coming.

items.body: MegaSoft: Verify your account

clues.why: The real domain is verify-account.app. 'megasoft.com-login' is a subdomain made to fool you.
